contexts.text: To vintage the clusters of the earth () = to destroy all things of charity. ( = to consume the truth and good of the Church. AC 9139:3.) (Compare AR 649. AR 650.)
Grape-gatherers () = falsities which are not from evil. AE 919:5.
To vintage, is to take down the vine and gather the grapes.
Vintage = the truth of the Church.
The truths of good that were taken away, are meant by the vintage... ().
The vintage that shall be consumed... () = no longer any truth of the Church; for vintage = the same as wine, namely, the truth of the Church.
Spiritual good, which is truth from celestial good, is signified by the vintage; and vastation is signified by the beating, and the gleanings, when the vintage is done ().
To put in the sharp sickle, and vintage () = to gather together the good, and separate them from the evil. Explained. AE 919.

To vintage = to collect for uses things which will be of service to the understanding, and will give intelligence and wisdom; and, in the opposite sense, to devastate the Church as to spiritual good, and thus as to the understanding and affection of truth. Vintage, and to vintage, are used in this opposite sense when there are no longer any clusters or grapes remaining; by which, in the spiritual sense, is signified that all spiritual good, and thus all truth which in itself is truth, has been destroyed...
Vintage = the good of spiritual love, which is love towards the neighbour.
